title: A smooth integral variety has a finite etale affine-space chart
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X/k$ be a smooth integral separated scheme of finite type [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. There exist integers $d\geq0$ and $n\geq1$, a nonempty affine open $V\subseteq\mathbf A^d_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-open-immersion], a nonempty dense affine open subscheme $j:W\hookrightarrow X$, and a finite etale surjective $k$-morphism $q:W\to V$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The morphism $q$ is finite locally free of constant degree $n$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For every $v\in V(k)$ its scheme fibre $W_v=W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is isomorphic over $k$ to a disjoint union of $n$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$; in particular its points are $n$ distinct $k$-rational points of $W$. Both $W$ and $V$ are smooth integral schemes of finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 054L, morphisms-lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; Tag 02NW, morphisms-lemma-generically-finite, (1) iff (4), shrinking its affine etale chart over the generic point; Tag 04MH, morphisms-lemma-finite-locally-free, constant rank on the integral target; Tag 02GL, morphisms-lemma-etale-over-field, split rational fibres. This is the W to V chart in groupoids.tex, lemma-algebraic-quasi-projective.

proof.text: Choose a point $x\in X$, which exists by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Apply [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $x$. Its target affine neighbourhood is all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so we obtain $d\geq0$, a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq X$ and an etale $k$-morphism $\pi:U\to A=\mathbf A^d_k$. The affine-space identification in [def-sbc-affine-space] gives $A=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for $R=k[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$.

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space, applied over the field; groupoids.tex Tag 0BF7, lemma-algebraic-quasi-projective, the diagram with U and W.

proof.text: The ring $R$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, with generators $t_1,\ldots,t_d$, so $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $k$; thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to conclude that $A$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; polynomial finite type follows from its displayed finite generators.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), $\pi$ is affine, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its etaleness makes it unramified and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The finite presentations of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] give finite generating sets, hence $\pi$ is locally of finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] every point is isolated in its fibre. Local finite type together with quasi-compactness is finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so this is quasi-finiteness [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Apply [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] to obtain finite set-theoretic fibres, in particular over every generic point of $A$.

source.place: Tags 02GI (definition-etale), 02V5 (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite), 02NH (lemma-quasi-finite) and 02NW (lemma-generically-finite), finite generic fibre hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] to $\pi$: step 2 supplies the Noetherian target, and step 3 supplies quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, local finite type and finite generic fibres. Obtain a dense open $O\subseteq A$ such that $\pi^{-1}O\to O$ is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], $\pi(U)$ is a nonempty open of $A$. Density of $O$ therefore gives a point $a\in O\cap\pi(U)$. The basic-open basis [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] gives $h\in R$ with $a\in D(h)\subseteq O\cap\pi(U)$. Put $V=D(h)$. It is affine, with ring $R_h$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b).

source.place: Tag 02NW, lemma-generically-finite, (1) implies (4), and Tag 03WT, lemma-etale-open; affine refinement by schemes basic opens, Tag 01HV.

proof.text: Put $W=\pi^{-1}V$, $q=\pi|_W:W\to V$, and let $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ be the composite open immersion through $U$. The open-preimage fibre-product assertion [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] makes $q$ a base change of $\pi^{-1}O\to O$. Thus $q$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], whose finite-morphism clause is independent of radiciality. It is etale by [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction]. Since $V\subseteq\pi(U)$, every point of $V$ has a preimage in $W$, so $q$ is surjective and $W$ is nonempty. Finiteness means affineness of the morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; with affine target $V$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2) makes $W$ affine.

source.place: Tag 01WL, lemma-base-change-finite, finite clause; Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize, etale restriction; groupoids.tex Tag 0BF7, W equal to the inverse image of V.

proof.text: The nonempty open $W$ of the integral scheme $X$ is integral: every nonempty affine open of $W$ is also a nonempty affine open of $X$, so its ring is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. It is dense because a nonempty open in an irreducible space meets every nonempty open. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain], $R$ is a domain. As $D(h)$ is nonempty, $h\neq0$, and $R_h$ is a nonzero domain: a product of fractions can vanish only when a numerator product vanishes. Consequently $V=\operatorname{Spec}R_h$ is integral by the domain-spectrum clause of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2).

source.place: Tags 01OK (definition-integral) and 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral), and schemes.tex Tag 01HV for the spectrum of a domain; elementary localization fraction computation.

proof.text: The finite etale $q$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant] its fibre dimension $\delta_q(v)=\dim_{\kappa(v)}\Gamma(W_v,\mathcal O_{W_v})$ is locally constant. It is constant on the nonempty irreducible $V$: two nonempty open level sets for different values would be disjoint, contrary to irreducibility. Call its value $n$. Each fibre is finite by base change [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], and is therefore the affine spectrum of its finite-dimensional coordinate algebra [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim]. Surjectivity makes every fibre nonempty: by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] the underlying space of $W_v$ is homeomorphic to $q^{-1}(v)\neq\emptyset$. If $n=0$, its coordinate algebra would be the zero vector space and the zero ring, with empty spectrum; this contradicts nonemptiness. Thus $n\geq1$, and the degree is constantly $n$.

source.place: Tags 02KB, lemma-finite-flat, and 04MH, lemma-finite-locally-free, on the integral target; the positivity follows from surjectivity.

proof.text: Let $v\in V(k)$. Its residue field is $k$: the residue-field map into $k$ induced by the rational point is a $k$-linear field embedding, hence surjective since its image contains $k$. The rational point $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$ has image $v$, so it factors through the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ by this isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\cong\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$; hence $W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the scheme fibre $W_v$ of [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to $q$ at $v$. It expresses $W_v$ over $k$ as a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions $L/k$. Each is $k$: an element has an irreducible minimal polynomial, which over the algebraically closed $k$ has a root, so that polynomial is linear. The finite fibre in [def-pc-finite-locally-free] therefore consists of some finite number $m$ of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The sheaf axiom on this disjoint cover gives global sections $k^m$, of dimension $m$; step 7 gives dimension $n$, so $m=n$. Its component points are distinct and their composites with $W_v\to W$ are distinct $k$-rational points, because [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies its underlying points bijectively with the points of $W$ mapping to $v$.

source.place: Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field, (2), over an algebraically closed residue field; degree computation by the product of n copies of k.

proof.text: Finally $W$ is smooth over $k$ by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] applied to $j$ and the given smooth $X/k$. The space $A$ is smooth over $k$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], so the same open-immersion lemma makes $V$ smooth. Its coordinate ring is $R_h= k[t_1,\ldots,t_d,z]/(hz-1)$, generated by the $d$ coordinates and $z$, so $V$ is of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $q$ is finite, its affine coordinate ring is a finite $R_h$-module [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Any finite module generating set is also an algebra generating set, so $q$ is of finite type. Composition [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) makes $W/k$ of finite type. Step 6 gave both integrality assertions and density, and steps 5, 7 and 8 give all the remaining clauses.
